correctness.rationale: Every pair of vertices has at most two common neighbors. The two explicit simplex/cone covers have the same nerve, and every nonempty intersection is a simplex or point, permitting two finite nerve-lemma applications. The constructed square-filled double cover has exactly two triangles per lifted square; the edge-disjointness hypothesis makes the stated free-face collapses valid without interference. Each of 2k discs uses two elementary collapses, leaving a graph with 2v vertices, 2e-2k edges and the original one/two parity components. Graph-cycle ranks yield the exact formulas. The deterministic verifier checks all 6,729 connected labeled single-four-cycle graphs on 4–6 vertices plus nine larger pairwise edge-disjoint-square examples; these finite checks supplement rather than prove the universal quantifier.

originality.rationale: The known square-free box-complex comparison explicitly excludes the positive-square regime; general fundamental-group results and neighborhood face polynomials do not determine higher homotopy; the known low-degree circle-wedge classification does not cover arbitrary vertex degree. The novel mathematical part is the square-filled double-cover good-cover nerve equivalence and simultaneous simplicial collapses for all graphs with pairwise edge-disjoint four-cycles. Unindexed equivalent approaches remain a risk.

value.rationale: This is a uniform structural classification for an unbounded natural family of graphs, permitting arbitrarily many edge-disjoint squares, vertex-sharing squares, arbitrary maximum degree, odd cycles and other topology. It identifies exactly when the open-neighborhood complex of such a graph is one or two wedges of circles, computes full integral homology, and provides a constructive common-neighbor nerve and finite simplicial-collapse mechanism. Known face polynomials and fundamental-group computations do not provide this homotopy result.
